structure:
A Playwright trace corpus of the animals frontend's fit suite (repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend, run at 4c2119da with --trace on, Playwright 1.63.0): 455 tests, all passed, one <test folder>/trace.zip each in workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/traces-animals-fit/. report.json in that folder is the Playwright JSON report (preceded by npm and webpack log lines) and maps every test to its trace folder; the full index (spec file, line, describe › test title, status, trace folder) is in distil/extract/trace-animals-fit.work/index.tsv. Two Playwright projects: "journeys" (fit/journey-smoke.fit.spec.js, 4 tests) and "features" (28 spec files under src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/, 451 tests). Tests per spec: journey-smoke 4, page-title 2, section-caption 5, service-navigation 7, dashboard 15, notification-actions 4, delete-notification 5, cancel-amend 5, hub 22, origin 33, import-reason 21, commodities/search 14, commodities/consignment-details 18, commodities/identification 46, additional-details 9, contact 6, cph-number 15, addresses/hub-picker 27, addresses/party-edit 5, transport/arrival-transit 39, transport/transporters 53, transport/commercial-transporter-details 27, documents/upload 28, documents/scan-status 4, documents/drop-zone 6, documents/guidance 4, check-answers 21, declaration 5, confirmation 5. Each fit test drives one feature page or a short run of pages against stubbed backends, so a trace shows the real frontend's rendered pages, copy, validation and redirects for that feature, not a whole journey. The scope takes in every trace; nothing is left out. The corpus covers only what the fit specs walk: the INS dashboard and address book (other repos) are not here, and a page or branch no fit test reaches leaves no trace. Cut into 26 parts in journey order, by spec file, with the seven largest specs (origin, identification, hub-picker, arrival-transit, transporters, commercial-transporter-details, upload) split on their describe blocks so no part holds more than 25 traces.

Extracted in 26 parts:
Part 1, Journey glue and shared page chrome: Part 1, journey glue and shared page chrome: 18 traces from four spec files, all opened and mined (the bundled trace CLI refuses these Playwright 1.63 zips with TraceVersionError, so each zip's extracted context trace, test trace and network log were read with jq in part1/; folder sizes were checked against the zip listing). journey-smoke.fit.spec.js (4 tests, project journeys): s1 = :31 entry guards and opening spine (9db27), s2 = :92 opening run to the review page (1ca52), s3 = :131 notification opened from another session (1beec), s4 = :153 change context from check answers (5e933). page-title.fit.spec.js (2): pt1 = :36 title pattern (2cd26), pt2 = :44 error prefix (b40e3). section-caption.fit.spec.js (5): sc1 = :52 consignment question (6b1ad), sc2 = :67 hidden-legend page (d7b0b), sc3 = :85 dashboard (a5814), sc4 = :96 overview bare (9e37a), sc5 = :104 axe with caption (b78a7). service-navigation.fit.spec.js (7): sn1 = :29 four items (da70d), sn2 = :35 dashboard current (e1a1f), sn3 = :43 current inside a notification (1a793), sn4 = :53 dashboard reachable from a notification (a40ce), sn5 = :72 sign-out href (e6c19), sn6 = :80 no signed-in user shown (1d6b5), sn7 = :91 axe on dashboard (b71ef). Pages walked, in order of the opening run (s2): stub sign-in, / redirect, dashboard /live-animals, POST /notifications creates the notification, origin, commodities (What are you importing?), consignment-details (Commodity details), import-reason, commodities/identification, additional-details, port-of-entry (Arrival details), transit-countries, transporters, accompanying-documents (Upload documents), addresses (Consignment addresses) with five party select pages, cph-number, consignment/contact/select, notification-view (Review your notification). Also walked: the overview (hub) at /notifications/<ref>, the origin page in its error state, the identification and documents pages in change mode (?change=1). Conditional: run mode (save chains to the next page) holds only until the user reaches the overview; additional details follows import reason; transit countries and transporters follow arrival details; cph-number follows addresses. Claims cover the journey glue (redirects, run mode, change context), the shared chrome on every page (title, header, service navigation, phase banner, footer, notification strip, caption, back link, button group), and each walked page's URL, title, caption and heading; each feature page's own fields, options and validation copy are left to that feature's part.
Part 2, Dashboard and notification actions: Part 2, Dashboard and notification actions. Read in full: dashboard.fit.spec.js (15 tests in 6 describes) and notification-actions.fit.spec.js (4 tests), and all 19 trace zips the part names. The zips were written by a newer Playwright than tim's trace viewer can open (TraceVersionError on `open`), so each trace was read from its unpacked folder in the part2 working folder (d01-d15 = the 15 dashboard traces in read order, n1-n4 = the 4 notification-actions traces; each folder's title was checked against its spec line). Rendered DOM came from the frame snapshots in each trace's 1-trace.trace, the action list from test.trace, and the network log from 1-trace.network. Pages in this slice, in journey order: (1) sign-in stub redirect into the dashboard; (2) the dashboard at /live-animals, seen empty (d01, d14), with one draft (d05, d06, d12, d15, n1), one submitted (d03, d04), one amending (d07), two drafts (d08, d10, n3), 21 drafts over two pages (d11), and with a no-match search (d09); (3) the origin page reached from Start a new notification (d02), and the origin page reopened on a copied draft (n2); (4) the notification overview (hub) reached after amend (d07), after copy (n1, n2, n4) and at the end of the start helper (d13). Conditional: row actions depend on status (Draft, Submitted, Amending); the empty text shows only with no notifications and no search; the no-match copy shows only with a search; pagination shows only above 20 rows. Delete and cancel-amend destinations are part 3 and were not followed here; the full journey pages the staging helpers walk through (commodities to declaration) belong to other parts and are only cited where they set up a dashboard state.
Part 3, Delete notification and cancel-amend: Part 3 of trace:animals-fit: the delete-notification and cancel-amend features of the live-animals frontend. Read in full: cancel-amend.fit.spec.js (5 tests) and delete-notification.fit.spec.js (4 tests in 'delete-notification feature', 1 in 'delete-notification feature (submitted)'), plus all 10 trace zips the partition names. The bundled `playwright trace open` refused these zips (TraceVersionError: created by a newer Playwright), so each zip was unpacked into the part3 working folder (c1-c5 = cancel-amend tests :68, :82, :95, :111, :117; d1-d5 = delete tests :29, :45, :58, :77, :118, confirmed against each trace's context title) and mined with jq: every test step from test.trace, every request from the *.network files, and rendered DOM from frame snapshots. Refs below cite '<spec>:<line> trace' plus the test-step id (pw:api@N / expect@N) or the snapshot call id. Pages and order. Delete (draft): dashboard card (Resume, Copy as new, Delete links) -> GET /notifications/{ref}/delete 'Delete this notification?' (Draft tag strip, Back to /live-animals) -> 'No, return to dashboard' (link to /live-animals, notification kept) or 'Yes, delete notification' (POST, 302 to /live-animals?deleted=1, success banner 'Notification deleted', card gone). Delete (submitted): full journey submitted, dashboard card (View, Amend, Copy as new, Delete) -> same confirmation page with Submitted tag strip -> confirm -> /live-animals?deleted=1 banner. Cancel-amend: submitted notification -> dashboard 'Amend' (POST /amend, 302 to the hub, Amending tag) -> edit origin internal reference to DiscardMe99 (save returns to hub) -> 'Review and submit' -> review page with Amending strip and 'Cancel amendment' link -> GET /cancel-amend 'Cancel this amendment?' (Back to notification-view) -> 'No, return to notification' (link back to review, amendment and changed value kept) or 'Yes, cancel amendment' (POST, 302 to notification-view?cancelled=1: Submitted strip, success banner, original reference Imports456GB restored, read-only: no Change links, Copy as new and Delete buttons). Three axe checks (delete page, cancel page, restored review) each recorded an empty violations list. Conditional: the Draft/Submitted/Amending tag on the strip follows notification state; the Cancel amendment link appears only while amending. Not reached by any trace in this part: error states (stale concurrency token, failed delete), cancelling with no changes, direct URL access in the wrong state, Welsh copy, and the backend calls behind delete and cancel (the trace records only browser-to-frontend traffic).
Part 4, Notification hub (task list): Part 4, Notification hub (task list). Read hub.fit.spec.js in full (22 tests: hub feature 10, commodity totals 5, the Commodity details row 2, the Review and submit button 5) and mined all 22 trace zips its read names. The trace CLI could not open them (TraceVersionError: traces were written by Playwright 1.63.0, newer than tim's viewer), so each zip was read from its unzipped copy in this part's working folder (h01..h22, verified against the zips' file listings and mapped to spec lines through test.trace stacks): the browser actions and selectors from 1-trace.trace, the network log from 1-trace.network, and the server-rendered HTML of every page from resources/*.html. Trace short names used in refs: h01=34521 (newly entered statuses), h02=86460 (Notification tasklist heading), h03=66a0b (every task opens), h04=9fabe (arrival details before a commodity), h05=14eb3 (commodity details while nothing chosen), h06=9ae69 (identification row absent), h07=9c588 (identification row appears), h08=9340d (section 2 order), h09=f896d (only one hint), h10=6b3c3 (no back link, return to dashboard), h11=e7523 (Commodity details row own task), h12=94963 (Commodity details Complete), h13=192df (review with only origin), h14=9699e (button group), h15=8fdf3 (review once all sections complete), h16=fed70 (single species, no identifier), h17=7b55a (axe, origin only), h18=1daf7 (totals read 0), h19=b80df (number, label, caption), h20=5829f (govuk design tokens), h21=5585e (small screen), h22=d269d (axe with totals). One page is in scope: the hub, GET /live-animals/notifications/{reference}, h1 'Overview'. Top to bottom it holds a journey strip (Draft tag and reference), the 'Your commodities' totals (two app-commodity-total boxes), the 'Notification tasklist' h2 over six numbered h3 sections each with its own govuk-task-list, and a button group (Review and submit, Return to dashboard). States seen: newly entered (origin only; 10 rows, no Identification details, no Transit countries), commodity chosen without numbers, commodity numbers saved, arrival details saved with no commodity (Transit countries appears), every section but documents complete (12 rows). Conditional rows: Identification details (once a commodity carrying identifiers is chosen) and Transit countries (once arrival details are saved). The pages the rows open were followed only as far as their heading and where saving them leads back; their contents belong to other parts.
Part 5, Origin: country, region and internal reference: Part 5 mined all 23 traces of origin.fit.spec.js in three describe blocks: 'origin feature' (12 tests, spec lines 106-308), 'origin country and region validation' (9 tests, lines 553-695) and 'origin internal reference validation' (2 tests, lines 728-750), plus the spec file itself for titles and assertions. Each trace zip had been unpacked into the part5 working folder (a01-a12 = origin feature in read order, v01-v09 = country and region validation, r01-r02 = internal reference validation); each folder's test title was confirmed from its 0-trace.trace before mining. For every trace the test-runner actions (test.trace), the DOM snapshots (1-trace.trace frame-snapshots, rendered with jq) and the network log (1-trace.network, including POST form bodies, status and Location) were read. No test step in any of the 23 traces recorded an error. Refs below name the trace by its zip hash (for example 'origin-f-184d5') and either the test step id (pw:api@N / expect@N) or the library snapshot call id (call@N). Pages reached, in order: dashboard /live-animals -> 'Start a new notification' POST /live-animals/notifications (302) -> origin page /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/origin ('Origin of the import', always first) -> on a valid save with a country, /commodities ('What are you importing?'); with no country, the notification hub /live-animals/notifications/{reference} ('Overview'). Also touched in passing: the hub (via Back and 'Cancel and return to overview'), the dashboard (via Back) and /notification-view ('Review your notification', only its origin rows are claimed here). Conditional surface: the region of origin code box is revealed only under 'Yes'; the fixed country prefix beside it appears only once a country value is held or submitted. Error states driven: out-of-list country, invalid region requirement option, Yes with empty code, code over 5 characters, internal reference over 58 characters; every error re-render answered HTTP 400. The country type-ahead's own behaviour (filtering, focus listing) is part 6 and is not claimed here beyond what these traces render.
Part 6, Origin: country type-ahead: Part 6, Origin: country type-ahead. Mined all 10 traces from origin.fit.spec.js: 'country of origin type-ahead' (5: bd485 on-focus list, 8a7ac case-insensitive filtering, 396be chosen country stays visible and submits its code, 52274 no-results message, 84b22 axe on the open list), 'country of origin type-ahead styles' (4: 2014a GOV.UK typography, 9bacc dropdown arrow paint order, 94eaa focus indicator, f489f error border), and 'country of origin without JavaScript' (1: 0141f native select submits and persists the code). The bundled trace CLI could not open these traces (TraceVersionError: recorded by Playwright 1.63.0, newer than the viewer tim installs), so each zip was unzipped into this part's work folder (part6/<hash>/) and read directly: browser calls and results from 1-trace.trace, test steps and assertion values from test.trace, the network log from 1-trace.network, server-rendered HTML and the application stylesheet from resources/. Refs give the trace's short hash and the call id (call@N, from 1-trace.trace) or step id (pw:api@N / expect@N, from test.trace). Every trace walks the same short path: stub sign-in (/auth/stub-sign-in?organisationId=stub-org-1), the dashboard /live-animals, the create-notification button (POST /live-animals/notifications, 302) and then the first journey page /live-animals/notifications/<GBN-AG-26-XXXXXX>/origin ('About the consignment' caption, 'Origin of the import' heading). Pages seen: Origin of the import (always; with JavaScript it carries the accessible-autocomplete type-ahead over the native select), its error state (f489f, POST 400 with an error summary), and What are you importing? (/commodities, reached after a successful save in 0141f). Only the country of origin field is in this slice; the region-of-origin and internal-reference fields appear here only as the page they sit on and are claimed lightly. Covered: the 40-country list on the select and in the open list, focus/click/type/select behaviour, filtering, the no-results row, the combobox ARIA wiring, the axe result on the open list, the asserted styles (font, size, arrow paint stack, focus outline, error border) with the stylesheet rules behind them, the out-of-list error, and the no-JavaScript save and re-display. Not reached, recorded as gaps: keyboard navigation of the list, Escape/blur behaviour, live-region announcement text, the type-ahead's handling of a previously saved value with JavaScript, the no-JavaScript error state, a narrow viewport, and the country reference-data call itself (server-side, never in the browser's network log).
Part 7, Import reason: Part 7, Import reason: the 21 traces of import-reason.fit.spec.js (describe 'import-reason feature' 6 tests, 'import-reason reveals' 10 tests, 'import-reason reveal accessibility' 5 tests), every one mined, plus the spec file for test titles and assertions. The playwright trace viewer tim installs refused these zips (TraceVersionError: trace created by a newer Playwright), so each zip, already unpacked in this part's working folder as r01..r21 in the partition's read order (checked against each trace's own title), was mined with jq straight from its 1-trace.trace (before/after action events and DOM frame snapshots) and 1-trace.network (requests, POST bodies, redirects). Refs name a trace by the five-hex hash in its folder name (traces-animals-fit/import-reason-import-reaso-<hash>-.../trace.zip) and its spec line, plus a call id. Every test reaches the page the same way: stub sign-in, start a notification at /live-animals, answer the origin page (France, No), then go straight to /live-animals/notifications/<ref>/import-reason. One page is in scope: 'Main reason for import' (caption 'About the consignment'), one visually hidden-legend radio group of five reasons, four of which open a conditional reveal: Internal market (purpose radios, 11 options), Transhipment or onward travel (destination country), Transit (port of exit, then destination country) and Temporary admission horses (exit date with an MOJ date picker, then port of exit); Re-entry opens none. States mined: first load (d35ea call@3215), reveals opened (9686e, a4fda, 5a9a5, 0d9f5, 37935), picker dialog open (31ec8, 5d7fa), error states (53e8f invalid reason, 71671 transit country missing, 92eb2 and 6c14b purpose missing, 637ba exit date missing, 4b0a1 date and port missing, ce728 port and country missing), save-and-revisit (5dffd, c6c14, 31ec8), back link (aa44e), and axe runs (e8003, 4b0a1, ce728, 0c220, 6c14b, 5d7fa). After a valid save the page redirects to the notification hub ('Overview'), whose task list was read once (5dffd call@3837) for this task's row. Nothing on the page is conditional except the reveals and the error state.
Part 8, Commodity search: Part 8, Commodity search. Read search.fit.spec.js (describe 'commodity search', 14 tests, lines 63 to 228) and mined all 14 trace zips it produced, one per test, in read order (working folders s01..s14 under trace-animals-fit.work/part8/ map to lines 63, 76, 95, 103, 116, 126, 138, 153, 159, 176, 181, 193, 216, 228). The playwright trace CLI that tim runs refused these traces (TraceVersionError: created by a newer Playwright), so each zip's extracted trace, network and frame-snapshot records were read directly with jq: every action (before events), every localhost request with its form body, status and redirect, and the full DOM snapshot of each distinct page state rendered from main. Every test shares one set-up: stub sign-in, Start a new notification, origin answered (France, No) and saved, then the overview link 'What are you importing?' opens the page. One page is in scope: 'What are you importing?' at /live-animals/notifications/{ref}/commodities (caption 'About the consignment'), always reached from the overview. Its states, all on that one URL: empty (s01, s02 help opened); short query, no results (s03); results grouped by commodity (s04, s05, s06, s07, s14); no match (s08); a running selection panel with Clear all (s09, s12, s13, s14); validation error on empty submit (s11). Save and continue leads to Commodity details (/consignment-details, s12, s13), seen only for its species headings; the back link returns to the overview (s10). The axe test (s14) passed with help open, one species chosen and two result groups showing. Claims record the page skeleton, every field, result and panel copy, the selection and save behaviour, the form posts that carry them, the validation, and gaps for controls no test drove.
Part 9, Commodity consignment details: Part 9, Commodity consignment details. Mined all 18 traces of consignment-details.fit.spec.js (10 in 'rendering and validation', 8 in 'persistence and accessibility'); the earlier extraction of each zip sits in the part9 working folder as c01..c18 in the partition's read order (c01=1e363 renders table, c02=644f1 heading sizes, c03=b8182 remove values, c04=f3deb back link, c05=18456 animals Bos taurus 2.5, c06=5467c packages Bos taurus 'boxes', c07=8233c animals Felis catus 0, c08=33681 packages Felis catus -1, c09=7f2a3 all blank, c10=32024 one blank, c11=b423b save and persist, c12=01f7a remove Cat, c13=fc0ef remove Cow, c14=68865 remove last, c15=499d8 add another, c16=86276 button group, c17=d6311 save and return, c18=55d05 axe). For each I read the full test-step list, the network log (data calls only) and the frame snapshots on /consignment-details, and dumped the main DOM tree, every input/button attribute and the error states. Every trace shares one set-up: stub sign-in, start a notification, answer origin (France, no region), open 'What are you importing?' from the overview, select Bos taurus (Cow, 0102) and Felis catus (Cat, 01061900), Save and continue, landing on 'Commodity details'. Pages in this slice: (1) Commodity details at /live-animals/notifications/{ref}/consignment-details, always reached after the commodity question and linked straight from the overview task 'Commodity details'; it has a 'Selected commodities' table form with per-row Remove buttons, an 'Add another commodity' link, then a quantities form with one H2 per commodity ('Cow (0102)'), one H3 per species, and per species 'Number of animals' and 'Number of packages (when required)'; then a button group (Save and continue, Save and return to overview, Cancel and return to overview). (2) Its error state (same URL, 200 re-render with error summary). Conditional surfaces: rows on code 01061900 carry a species-level remove; removing the last line, or opening the page with nothing selected, redirects to 'What are you importing?'. Exits observed: Save and continue and Save and return to overview both 302 to the overview; back link to the overview. The overview task list and totals were read only where these traces land on it after saving. Not reached: Cancel and return to overview was asserted visible but never clicked; no trace drove zero or blank packages alone, upper limits, mixed errors across fields, or a concurrency conflict.
Part 10, Animal identification: page, records and summary: Part 10 mined all 25 traces of identification.fit.spec.js in its four in-scope describe blocks: 'animal identification' (12 tests: :245 dd986, :278 b2d23, :305 19c03, :320 bfdf8, :335 b2ce6, :357 fe9ed, :380 66033, :394 e3b1e, :403 b2704, :427 fab50, :432 a2cb0, :447 dcde6), 'in-card save button' (3: :473 05b15, :503 a783b, :533 4fc89), 'selected commodities summary' (3: :553 7044e, :585 e7929, :600 d6eef) and 'records' (7: :723 07a52, :764 26bc8, :795 d1d4b, :818 285e7, :824 8b38b, :835 fdf5c, :853 0e965). The trace CLI refused every zip (TraceVersionError: trace made by a newer Playwright than tim's viewer), so each zip's extracted raw files (already unpacked under the part10 working folder as t01..t25, one per read entry in order, each confirmed by its recorded test title) were read with jq: every 'before' call event for the action list, frame-snapshots rendered to the DOM of <main> at the identification page, and resource-snapshots for the network log (crumb values redacted). Every trace walks the same set-up: stub sign-in, Start a new notification, Origin of the import (France, No), Overview, What are you importing? (search and tick one or more species), Commodity details (number of animals per line), Overview, then the 'Identification details' task row into the page under test. Pages reached: Overview (task row 'Identification details' under '2. Description of the goods', absent when nothing is identifiable), Identification details at /live-animals/notifications/{ref}/commodities/identification (always the subject), Commodity details at /consignment-details (via Change number of animals and the count-drop error), What are you importing? at /commodities (via Change and Add another commodity). Identification page skeleton in order: journey strip (Draft tag, notification reference), caption 'About the consignment', h1 'Identification details', inset text, 'Selected commodities' summary table (code, common name, number of animals, Change link), 'Add another commodity' link, then one form holding a visually hidden 'Save and finish' submit, one card section per identifiable commodity line (h2 '<Common> (<code>) — <species>', Change number of animals link, saved-animals table once a record exists, h3 'Enter details for <species> N of M', identifier inputs in the commodity's own order, for cat and dog a fraud warning, permanent-address guidance and eight address inputs, an in-card secondary button 'Save and add another' or 'Save and finish' when the line holds more than one animal), then the button group (Save and continue, Save and return to overview, Cancel and return to overview). Species walked: cattle (Bos taurus: ear tag, passport), horse (Equus caballus: microchip, passport, horse name), cat (Felis catus: microchip, passport, tattoo plus permanent address), dog (Canis lupus familiaris: same as cat), salmon (Salmo salar: no identifiers, no card). Identifier and address validation are part 11 and are not claimed here; the count-drop and stale-add cap errors fall in this slice's records tests and are claimed.
Part 11, Animal identification: identifier and address validation: Part 11 mined all 21 traces of identification.fit.spec.js's two validation describes: 'animal identification identifier validation' (7 tests: the empty-record test at line 619, the five 58-character identifier tests at line 636 for Microchip, Tattoo, Passport, Ear tag and Horse name, and the microchip error-state axe test at line 653) and 'animal identification address validation' (14 tests: six empty-mandatory-field tests at line 681 and eight over-length tests at line 700). The spec file was read in full for test titles and assertions. The traces were written by a newer Playwright than tim's trace viewer supports (tim distil trace open fails with TraceVersionError), so each zip's already-unpacked contents in the part11 working folder were read with jq: the test.trace action list, the page's final frame snapshot holding the error summary, and the network log's POST to the identification page. Every trace walks the same set-up (stub sign-in, start a notification, country of origin, 'What are you importing?', species, animal count on consignment details, then the overview's 'Identification details' link) to one page, /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/commodities/identification, headed 'Identification details', which re-renders with an error summary after a POST. Three commodity cards appear across the traces: Cat (01061900) — Felis catus (microchip, passport, tattoo, plus the permanent address block of eight fields), Cow (0102) — Bos taurus (ear tag, passport, no address block) and Horse (0101) — Equus caballus (microchip, passport, horse name, no address block). Conditional surface: the in-card 'Save and add another' button appears only when the line's count is above one (count 2 cat traces) and is absent on count-1 lines; the address block appears only on the cat card. Every error page showed exactly one error. All 21 tests passed; the axe test recorded no serious or critical violations. No network call other than the page's own GET and POST is visible in the browser's log.
Part 12, Additional details and contact: Part 12 (Additional details and contact) mined all 15 traces its read names: 9 from additional-details.fit.spec.js (rendering: 98ff4 :43, 7551a :74, be2d3 :83; unweaned commodity gate: a90fd :101, 01f6b :112; validation: db17f :139, c0bef :169; persistence and accessibility: 95b78 :208, 42575 :227) and 6 from contact.fit.spec.js (3ac7c :43, d776d :60, 6b476 :66, 6aea6 :89, c6038 :117, a6bde :125). Both spec files were read in full for test titles and assertions. Method note: the trace CLI run through `tim distil trace` refused every zip (TraceVersionError: the traces were recorded by a newer Playwright than the viewer tim installs), so each zip, already unzipped into this part's working folder by an earlier run, was read directly: the action timeline from the `before` events of 1-trace.trace, the rendered DOM from the largest frame-snapshot for a call (rendered to markup with a jq filter), the page title and back link from the same snapshot, the form posts and redirects from 1-trace.network, and the axe result from the `after` event of the axe finishRun call. Action ids below are those callIds. Pages, in journey order: (1) Additional details, /live-animals/notifications/{ref}/additional-details, caption 'Commodity details', h1 'Additional details', task row 'Additional details' under '2. Description of the goods' on the Overview hub. Two radio questions under one h1: 'What are the animals certified for?' (16 options, always asked) and 'Does the consignment contain any unweaned animals?' (Yes/No, asked of cattle (Bos taurus) and not of a horses-only (Equus caballus) consignment). Every trace reached it by direct navigation after origin, commodity selection and commodity details. (2) Contact address for consignment, /live-animals/notifications/{ref}/consignment/contact/select, single-question page whose legend is the h1, task row 'Contact address for this consignment' under '6. Contact address'. One radio question listing 13 address-book contacts, each with its address as a radio hint; once a contact is saved, a 'Current contact address' summary card with an 'Edit details' link appears. Every contact trace reached it by direct navigation after only the origin page. Both pages post back to themselves (POST, 302 to the Overview hub on success, 400 with an error summary on an invalid value), carry a hidden concurrencyToken, and offer 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' and 'Cancel and return to overview'. Both are entirely govuk-frontend components apart from the app-journey-strip (Draft tag and notification reference).
